# Command reference

Local AI model server and manager

```text
alkahest [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

## Global options

Every command accepts these (`serve` binds `--host`, the client commands target it).

```text
      --host <HOST[:PORT]>  Server address: binds `serve`, targets client commands. Accepts `host`, `host:port`, `:port` or a URL. Overrides `ALKAHEST_HOST` and the configuration file
      --config <FILE>       Configuration file to use on top of the system and user files
  -v, --verbose...          More log output: `-v` debug, `-vv` trace
      --log-level <LEVEL>   Log level or filter directive; beats `-v` and the configuration file
      --json                Machine-readable JSON output where the command supports it
  -h, --help                Print help
  -V, --version             Print version
```

| [`completions`](#alkahest-completions) | Print a shell completion script to stdout |

## alkahest completions

Print a shell completion script to stdout

```text
alkahest completions [OPTIONS] <SHELL>
```

Arguments:

```text
  <SHELL>  Target shell [possible values: bash, elvish, fish, powershell, zsh]
```

## alkahest pull

Download a model from the Ollama registry or Hugging Face

```text
alkahest pull [OPTIONS] <MODEL>
```

Arguments:

```text
  <MODEL>  Model reference, for example `llama3.2:3b` or `hf.co/org/repo:Q4_K_M`
```

Options (besides the global ones):

```text
      --insecure            Talk to the registry over plain HTTP (private registries without TLS)
      --force               Download into the Alkahest store even when the Ollama store already has the model [alias: --copy]
      --safetensors         Download the safetensors snapshot of a Hugging Face repository for vLLM instead of GGUF (chosen automatically when the repository has no GGUF files)
```

## alkahest search

Search the Ollama library and Hugging Face for models

```text
alkahest search [OPTIONS] [QUERY]...
```

Arguments:

```text
  [QUERY]...
          Search terms
```

Options (besides the global ones):

```text
      --source <SOURCE>
          Where to search

          Possible values:
          - all:    Hugging Face and the Ollama library
          - hf:     Hugging Face only
          - ollama: The Ollama library only
          
          [default: all]
      --gguf
          Hugging Face: only GGUF repositories (the default)
      --safetensors
          Hugging Face: only safetensors repositories
      --all
          Hugging Face: do not filter by file format
      --task <TASK>
          Hugging Face: restrict to a task (pipeline tag), for example `text-generation`
      --sort <SORT>
          Hugging Face: sort order

          Possible values:
          - downloads: Most downloaded first
          - likes:     Most liked first
          - recent:    Recently updated first
          
          [default: downloads]
      --limit <N>
          Maximum results per source
          
          [default: 20]
  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## alkahest show

Show details of a model

```text
alkahest show [OPTIONS] <MODEL>
```

Arguments:

```text
  <MODEL>  Model reference: a name, `ollama:<name>`, `hf.co/org/repo:Q4_K_M`, a digest or the first characters of the `ID` column
```

Options (besides the global ones):

```text
      --modelfile           Print a Modelfile that recreates the model
      --template            Print only the prompt template
      --parameters          Print only the default parameters
      --license             Print only the licence
      --system              Print only the system prompt
```

## alkahest cp

Copy a model under a new name

```text

```

Arguments:

```text
  <SOURCE>       Existing model
  <DESTINATION>  New name
```

## alkahest run

Chat with a model interactively, or answer one prompt.

With a prompt, or with input piped on stdin, prints one answer and exits; otherwise opens an interactive session (`/?` for help, `/bye` to leave). Needs a running server (`alkahest serve`). For this command `--verbose` prints timing statistics after each answer instead of raising the log level.

```text
alkahest run [OPTIONS] <MODEL> [PROMPT]...
```

Arguments:

```text
  <MODEL>
          Model reference
  [PROMPT]...
          One-shot prompt (words are joined with spaces, after any piped input)
```

Options (besides the global ones):

```text
      --format <FORMAT>
          Response format: `json`, or a JSON schema
      --think [<WHEN>]
          Thinking for models that support it: `true`/`false`, or `high`/`medium`/`low`. `--think` alone means `true`
      --hidethinking
          Do not print the model's thinking (it still thinks when `--think` asks for it)
      --keepalive <DURATION>
          How long the model stays loaded after the last request (`5m`, `1h`, `0`, `-1`)
      --no-start
          Do not offer to start the server when it is not running
  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## alkahest serve

Start the API server

```text
alkahest serve [OPTIONS]
```

Options (besides the global ones):

```text
      --allow-unauthenticated  Start on a non-loopback address even though remote clients would not need a key (`auth.require_key_for_remote = false`) or no API key exists yet
```

## alkahest desktop

Open the desktop app (needs a build with the `desktop` feature)

```text
alkahest desktop [OPTIONS]
```

Options (besides the global ones):

```text
      --smoke-test          Open the window, wait for the first frame to be rendered, then exit with status 0 (used by CI; fails with status 3 when no frame arrives within 30 s)
```

## alkahest hf

Manage the Hugging Face token (`login`, `logout`, `whoami`)

```text
alkahest hf [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

| Subcommand | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `login` | Store a Hugging Face token in the OS keyring. The token is read from stdin (a prompt without echo on a terminal, one line when piped) and never printed |
| `logout` | Remove the stored token from the OS keyring |
| `whoami` | Show the account the current token belongs to |

### alkahest hf login

Store a Hugging Face token in the OS keyring. The token is read from stdin (a prompt without echo on a terminal, one line when piped) and never printed

```text
alkahest hf login [OPTIONS]
```

Options (besides the global ones):

```text
      --no-verify           Store the token without checking it against the Hub first
```

### alkahest hf logout

Remove the stored token from the OS keyring

```text
alkahest hf logout [OPTIONS]
```

### alkahest hf whoami

Show the account the current token belongs to

```text
alkahest hf whoami [OPTIONS]
```

## alkahest keys

Manage API keys

```text
alkahest keys [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

| Subcommand | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ls` | List keys [alias: list] |
| `create` | Create a key and print it once; only a salted hash is stored |
| `revoke` | Revoke a key; the next request with it is refused |

### alkahest keys ls

List keys

```text
alkahest keys ls [OPTIONS]
```

### alkahest keys create

Create a key and print it once; only a salted hash is stored

```text
alkahest keys create [OPTIONS] <NAME>
```

Arguments:

```text
  <NAME>  Label of the new key (unique among active keys)
```

Options (besides the global ones):

```text
      --scope <SCOPE>       Scope to grant: `inference` (default) or `admin` (includes inference). Repeatable
      --model <MODEL>       Restrict the key to this model. Repeatable; default: every model
      --expires <WHEN>      Expiry: a duration such as `12h`, `30d`, `8w`, or an RFC 3339 time
```

### alkahest keys revoke

Revoke a key; the next request with it is refused

```text
alkahest keys revoke [OPTIONS] <ID>
```

Arguments:

```text
  <ID>  Key id (`abcd1234` or `alk_abcd1234`) or active key name
```

## alkahest engines

Manage inference engines

```text
alkahest engines [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

| Subcommand | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ls` | List installed and available engines [alias: list] |
| `install` | Download and install an engine from its recipe |
| `rm` | Remove an installed engine version [alias: remove] |
| `info` | Show an engine's versions, variants, requirements and what is installed |

### alkahest engines ls

List installed and available engines

```text
alkahest engines ls [OPTIONS]
```

### alkahest engines install

Download and install an engine from its recipe

```text
alkahest engines install [OPTIONS] <ENGINE>
```

Arguments:

```text
  <ENGINE>  Engine id (`alkahest engines ls` lists them)
```

Options (besides the global ones):

```text
      --variant <VARIANT>         Accelerator build (`cpu`, `cuda12.8`, `cuda12`, `vulkan`, ...); the best one for this machine when omitted
      --version <ENGINE_VERSION>  Engine version to install; the newest one when omitted. Several versions can be installed side by side
      --from-source               Build from the recipe's source steps (needs git, cmake and ninja) instead of downloading the prebuilt archive
      --force                     Reinstall even when the engine is already installed
      --with-runtime              Also unpack the CUDA runtime libraries (cudart, cublas; 150 to 600 MB) next to the engine, for a CUDA build on a machine without a system-wide CUDA runtime
```

### alkahest engines rm

Remove an installed engine version

```text
alkahest engines rm [OPTIONS] <ENGINE>
```

Arguments:

```text
  <ENGINE>  Engine id
```

Options (besides the global ones):

```text
      --version <ENGINE_VERSION>  Version to remove; every installed version when omitted
      --variant <VARIANT>         Variant to remove; every installed variant when omitted
```

### alkahest engines info

Show an engine's versions, variants, requirements and what is installed

```text
alkahest engines info [OPTIONS] <ENGINE>
```

Arguments:

```text
  <ENGINE>  Engine id
```

## alkahest certs

Manage TLS certificates for HTTPS (`[server.tls]`)

```text
alkahest certs [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

| Subcommand | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `generate` | Write a self-signed server certificate, its key (owner only) and the CA clients trust to the `[server.tls]` paths (default `<data_dir>/tls/`) |

### alkahest certs generate

Write a self-signed server certificate, its key (owner only) and the CA clients trust to the `[server.tls]` paths (default `<data_dir>/tls/`)

```text
alkahest certs generate [OPTIONS]
```

Options (besides the global ones):

```text
      --name <NAME>         Extra DNS name or IP address the certificate must cover (localhost, the loopback addresses and this host's name are always included). Repeatable
      --days <DAYS>         Validity in days (at most 825, the limit Apple platforms accept) [default: 397]
      --force               Replace existing files
```

## alkahest service

Install or control the background service

```text
alkahest service [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

| Subcommand | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `install` | Install the service unit and start it |
| `uninstall` | Stop the service and remove the unit (the service user and its data stay) |
| `start` | Start the installed service |
| `stop` | Stop the installed service |
| `status` | Show whether the service is running and where it listens |

### alkahest service install

Install the service unit and start it

```text
alkahest service install [OPTIONS]
```

Options (besides the global ones):

```text
      --user
          Manage a per-user service (systemd `--user` unit, launchd LaunchAgent) instead of the system service
      --dry-run
          Print the unit and the commands without writing or running anything
      --root <DIR>
          Write below this directory and run no command (packaging, tests)
      --bin <PATH>
          Binary the unit starts; defaults to the running executable
      --manager <MANAGER>
          Service manager to target; defaults to this platform's. Another platform's manager only works with `--dry-run` or `--root` (packaging, review)

          Possible values:
          - systemd: systemd (Linux)
          - launchd: launchd (macOS)
          - windows: The Windows service control manager
  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

### alkahest service uninstall

Stop the service and remove the unit (the service user and its data stay)

## alkahest config

Inspect the effective configuration

```text
alkahest config [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

| Subcommand | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `show` | Print the effective configuration and where each layer came from |
| `path` | Print the configuration file locations and whether they exist |
| `model` | Show or edit the configuration overlay of one model |

### alkahest config show

Print the effective configuration and where each layer came from

```text
alkahest config show [OPTIONS]
```

### alkahest config path

Print the configuration file locations and whether they exist

```text
alkahest config path [OPTIONS]
```

### alkahest config model

Show or edit the configuration overlay of one model

```text
alkahest config model [OPTIONS] <MODEL> [COMMAND]
```

| Subcommand | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `show` | Print the overlay, the recommended defaults and the effective settings |
| `set` | Set one or more settings, `key=value` (for example `num_ctx=8192 kv_cache_type_k=q8_0`) |
| `unset` | Remove settings from the overlay |
| `path` | Print the path of the overlay file (edit it by hand if you prefer) |

Arguments:

```text
  <MODEL>  Model reference (an installed model, or a name to configure ahead of its pull)
```

#### alkahest config model show

Print the overlay, the recommended defaults and the effective settings

```text
alkahest config model <MODEL> show [OPTIONS]
```

#### alkahest config model set

Set one or more settings, `key=value` (for example `num_ctx=8192 kv_cache_type_k=q8_0`)

```text
alkahest config model <MODEL> set [OPTIONS] <KEY=VALUE>...
```

Arguments:

```text
  <KEY=VALUE>...  Assignments
```

#### alkahest config model unset

Remove settings from the overlay

```text
alkahest config model <MODEL> unset [OPTIONS] <KEYS>...
```

Arguments:

```text
  <KEYS>...  Setting names
```

#### alkahest config model path

Print the path of the overlay file (edit it by hand if you prefer)

```text
alkahest config model <MODEL> path [OPTIONS]
```
